title: "The Best Session So Far!" (Reflection From Our Third Live Session On Using Gemini Gems)
author: Dr Dario Emanuele
summary: Dario Emanuele's recap of his third live workshop goes well beyond event chatter to teach the NPPPN example sequence and show teachers how to automate it with a custom Gemini Gem. He grounds the sequence (Negative, Positive, Positive, Positive, Negative) in Engelmann's Theory of Instruction, Craig Barton's Tips for Teachers and Kris Boulton's atomisation work, and explains the role of each item: a near-boundary non-example, a minimally varied positive, maximally varied positives, and a final minimally varied negative. A key move, drawn from discussion in the session, separates the modelling phase, where the fixed NPPPN pattern scaffolds concept boundaries, from the testing phase, where the pattern must be randomised so students cannot game the rhythm. The article then gives a step-by-step workflow for building the Gem, including writing the instructional persona, encoding the variation rules, using Gemini's rewrite tool and setting output to Canvas, and appends the author's full Gem prompt. It closes by insisting that teacher expertise must come first: concepts should be atomised by hand before the AI is asked to execute the sequence.
points: NPPPN structures concept teaching as a binary question answered No, Yes, Yes, Yes, No, with minimal variation at the boundaries and maximal variation across the positive examples.

The first non-example should sit just outside the concept's boundary, and the final one should break a single defining rule of a heavily varied positive to check students are genuinely evaluating rather than defaulting to 'Yes'.
The fixed NPPPN order suits modelling only; for quizzes and independent checks the sequence must be randomised because students quickly learn and game the pattern.

The build workflow covers creating a new Gem, defining an instructional-designer persona, encoding minimal and maximal variation rules, rewriting with the Magic Wand and switching output to Canvas, plus a duplicate Gem for randomised testing.
Emanuele warns that the Gem cannot replace pedagogical intuition: teachers should map a concept's sub-skills and boundary rules on paper before directing the AI.
quotes: Every teacher eventually gets to know there is no single “silver bullet” in pedagogy. Instead, a truly effective practitioner possesses a toolbox full of silver bullets, selecting the exact right tool for the exact right moment.

This framework is deeply rooted in Siegfried Engelmann’s seminal Theory of Instruction (1982), which champions the power of teaching concepts through highly structured comparative sequences of examples and non-examples. It has been refined in contemporary maths pedagogy through Craig Barton’s Tips for Teachers framework, and is foundational to the categorical atomisation models developed by Kris Boulton at Unstoppable Learning.
You take the fully varied positive example and subtly break one defining rule. This tests whether students are genuinely evaluating the concept or just getting comfortable saying “Yes”.

If you maintain the NPPPN structure during independent checks or quizzes, students will quickly adapt to the underlying rhythm. They will notice the pattern (“Oh, it’s always No, Yes, Yes, Yes, No” or alternating yes-no-yes-no) and begin gaming the sequence without actually processing the properties of the examples.

Therefore, for the testing phase, the sequence must be completely jumbled or randomised (e.g., generating sequences like NPNPP or random distributions of positives and negatives). This forces students to independently evaluate every single problem on its own merit.
Once your instructions are pasted, click the Magic Wand (Rewrite) icon. Gemini will restructure your text into a clean, system-optimised prompt that ensures high fidelity to your rules.

As practitioners, we must build our own confidence with atomisation manually, mapping out concepts on a piece of paper first to truly understand where students stumble. Once you are completely clear on the microscopic sub-skills and boundary rules of a topic, you can direct Gemini to execute the sequence with absolute precision.
